name: Mesial Temporal Lobe Epilepsy with Hippocampal Sclerosis

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: International League Against Epilepsy (ILAE) criteria for MTLE-HS

criteria.description: Presence of focal seizures with impaired awareness, often with aura such as epigastric rising sensation or déjà vu
Electroencephalogram showing interictal epileptiform discharges localized to the mesial temporal lobe
MRI evidence of hippocampal atrophy and increased T2/FLAIR signal consistent with hippocampal sclerosis
Memory impairment consistent with temporal lobe dysfunction

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Clinical focal seizures with impaired awareness plus either ictal EEG abnormalities localized to mesial temporal lobe or MRI evidence of hippocampal sclerosis
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Definitive diagnosis may require video-EEG monitoring and neuroimaging correlation.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Focal impaired awareness seizures with epigastric aura
pathognomonic.notes: Characteristic rising epigastric sensation preceding seizures
searchTerms: seizures with impaired awareness and stomach aura
partial seizures with rising abdominal sensation

pathognomonic.notes: Repetitive involuntary movements such as lip-smacking or hand fumbling

common.symptomName: Memory impairment, particularly verbal memory deficits
common.notes: Often related to dominant temporal lobe involvement

common.symptomName: Aura of déjà vu or jamais vu
common.notes: Subjective feelings of familiarity or unfamiliarity
searchTerms: feeling of familiarity or unfamiliarity before seizure
déjà vu or jamais vu aura

occasional.notes: Perception of unpleasant smells during seizures

occasional.symptomName: Anxiety or panic attacks preceding seizures
occasional.notes: Emotional symptoms as part of aura

rare.symptomName: Autonomic symptoms such as tachycardia or flushing

laboratory: Routine blood tests typically normal; used to exclude metabolic causes
imaging: MRI showing hippocampal atrophy and increased T2/FLAIR signal in mesial temporal lobe
FDG-PET may show hypometabolism in affected temporal lobe
genetic: No specific genetic mutation identified; familial cases reported but rare
other: Video-EEG monitoring demonstrating ictal onset in mesial temporal structures

distinguishingFeatures: Seizure onset localized to lateral temporal neocortex rather than mesial structures
Different aura characteristics and MRI findings
Variable seizure semiology and psychological triggers

redFlags: Sudden onset of frequent generalized tonic-clonic seizures
Progressive neurological deficits or cognitive decline
Failure to respond to appropriate antiepileptic drug therapy
references: Engel J Jr. Mesial temporal lobe epilepsy: what have we learned? Neuroscientist. 2001;7(4):340-52.
Wiebe S, Blume WT, Girvin JP, Eliasziw M. A randomized, controlled trial of surgery for temporal-lobe epilepsy. N Engl J Med. 2001;345(5):311-8.
